CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for this package.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md @.claude/shared/native-code.md @.claude/shared/correctness.md @.claude/shared/assurance.md

What this is

zuproto decodes and encodes Protocol Buffers messages in R through upb, the small C runtime under protobuf’s Python, Ruby and PHP implementations. It works from descriptor sets (protoc --descriptor_set_out, buf build), not generated code: one message becomes a named list, many messages become a data frame built column by column. It also converts to and from protobuf’s canonical JSON, and packs and unpacks Any. It is a format package in the zu* family, like zucbor and zumsgpack, except that every call names a message type in a descriptor pool. upb and utf8_range are vendored, so there is no system protobuf, protoc or Abseil. Hard runtime dependencies are zero: no Imports, no LinkingTo; zuint and bit64 are in Suggests for 64-bit fields. It will not generate R code per message type, parse .proto or text format, or speak gRPC.

The specification is .agents/design.md, adopted from RFC 0010. It outranks this file: CLAUDE.md orients, the design doc decides. Its open questions (§18) are still open.

Current state

Verified 2026-11-11. Every stage of the roadmap in .agents/roadmap.md is merged, and v0.1.0 was submitted to CRAN on 2026-11-06 (CRAN-SUBMISSION); it is in the incoming queue. Later work is filed as enhancement issues (a .proto compiler, text format, TFRecord framing, proto_equal() and others), plus #128, a upb JSON UTF-8 fix for the next re-vendor.

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is #1 for v0.1.0; the CRAN-submission issue is #13. Sibling packages that depend on this one before CRAN does: none, and zuproto has no C API.

Commands

Run from the package root.

tools/verify-vendor                              # vendor, wkt.binpb, shim
tools/make-test-descriptors                      # after editing fixtures/proto/

tools/vendor-upb, tools/make-test-descriptors and the fixtures need protoc (brew install protobuf).

Occasional, for C changes and before a release:

tools/run-fuzz 60                                # fuzz targets, ASan + UBSan
CANARY_ONLY=1 tools/run-fuzz                     # every canary must crash
CONFORMANCE_RUNNER=<path> tools/conformance/run  # protobuf conformance suite
R CMD INSTALL . && tools/run-benchmarks          # design section 16

The conformance runner is built from protobuf at the vendored tag with CMake (-Dprotobuf_BUILD_CONFORMANCE=ON); .github/workflows/conformance.yaml shows how. The runner matches each expected failure’s message, so after a change that alters how a listed test fails, regenerate the list with tools/conformance/update-failure-list.py. After changing fixtures, run Rscript tools/fuzz/make-fuzz-data.R to refresh the fuzz seeds and tools/fuzz/data.h.

Architecture

.agents/design.md §4 has the whole plan.

  • src/zpb_upb.h is the shim: the only file that includes src/vendor/upb/ruby-upb.h or names a upb symbol. Everything else uses its zpb_ types and static inline wrappers. tools/verify-vendor fails on a leak.
  • C returns, R raises. .Call entry points (src/zpb.h, registered in src/init.c) return a value or an error string; R/ turns that into a classed condition with zpb_abort() (R/conditions.R). C calls Rf_error() only for out-of-memory and broken internal invariants.
  • Pools (R/pool.R, src/zpb_pool.c): a list of the external pointer to upb’s upb_DefPool and an environment of the files added, name to bytes. R checks a whole set (conflicts, missing imports, dependency order) before C adds any file. Every pool starts from inst/descriptors/wkt.binpb.
  • Decoding (R/decode.R, src/zpb_decode.c, src/zpb_build.c): upb decodes into an arena on a counting allocator (the 4 * max_size ceiling), held with that allocator by one finalised external pointer. Building R values starts only after a successful decode and walks the message by reflection. A value R cannot hold sets ctx->err, and every builder then returns NULL with its PROTECTs undone; warnings are counted in ctx and raised once by R.
  • Encoding (R/encode.R, src/zpb_fill.c): the R value is walked against the message definition and set on a upb message, then upb encodes. A wrong value stops the walk with an error code, a detail and the field’s path (ctx->path), which R raises. Strings handed to upb point into R memory, valid until the .Call returns.
  • Data frames (R/frame.R, build_frame() in src/zpb_build.c, zpb_decode_df() in src/zpb_decode.c): all messages are decoded into one arena, then each column is filled across all rows. rows[i] may be NULL (a nested message the parent row lacks), which makes that row NA. Delimited framing is in C; R reads connections in chunks for each.
  • JSON and Any (R/json.R, design §5 and §6.3): upb converts between binary and JSON; R checks arguments and raises. An Any converts only when the type it packs is in the pool.
  • Message fixtures come from Python protobuf 7.36.2 through tools/make-fixtures.py (it says how to set up the venv), stored as hex in tests/testthat/fixtures/msg/ with a MANIFEST.tsv.
  • Test fixtures are protoc output: edit tests/testthat/fixtures/proto/*.proto, run tools/make-test-descriptors, commit the .binpb files.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • All upb calls go through src/zpb_upb.h. No other file includes the vendored header, and tools/verify-vendor enforces it. Otherwise a re-vendor, against upb’s unstable API, means edits all over src/.
  • Never call R while upb is on the C stack. upb uses setjmp/longjmp for decoder errors; an R error unwinding through those frames skips its cleanup. Build R values only after upb_Decode returns kUpb_DecodeStatus_Ok, and never from a partly decoded message.
  • upb memory is owned by finalised external pointers. Each decode arena is wrapped from the moment it is created, so an interrupt during the R build phase frees it. No upb pointer is stored in an R object any other way, and strings are copied into CHARSXPs, never aliased.
  • Descriptor sets are trusted, message bytes are not. Every limit (max_size, max_depth, max_rows, the arena byte ceiling) and UTF-8 validation applies to message bytes.
  • Vendored patches are only those in the design (§9.2). Each one is listed there with its reason, and each upb bug it works around is reported upstream. A patch that touches decoder logic is a reason to stop and report upstream.
  • A builder that fails returns NULL with its PROTECTs undone, never Rf_error(): the entry point must hand the error back to R to raise with its class. Only out-of-memory and broken internal invariants call Rf_error() directly.
  • Iterators start at ZPB_*_ITER_BEGIN, not 0. upb’s begin values are (size_t) -1; 0 is a valid position.
  • Internal native symbols use zpb_ / ZPB_, not zuproto_. This is a deliberate deviation from the package-prefix rule in .claude/shared/r-package.md. R_init_zuproto is the only exported symbol (hidden visibility from Stage 0).

Testing

  • Conformance. The oracle is protobuf’s conformance_test_runner, run against an R testee (tools/conformance/) through the binary and JSON suites, in CI only. Its expected-failure lists (tools/conformance/failure_list.txt, text_format_failure_list.txt) may only shrink: the run fails on a test that fails outside the list, or on a listed one that passes.
  • Fixtures come from Python’s protobuf and protoc --encode, never by hand. They are written by tools/make-test-descriptors (protoc) and tools/make-fixtures.py (Python’s protobuf), with provenance and SHA-256 in fixtures/DESCRIPTORS.tsv and fixtures/msg/MANIFEST.tsv.
  • Helpers. helper-fixtures.R loads the committed fixtures (fixture(), msg_fixture(), decode_pool(), varint()); helper-entry-points.R has the table of entry points the shared argument tests walk.
  • Runtime. The design’s target is under 15 s; it ran in 10.6 s installed when last measured (2026-11-05).
  • Dev builds differ from installed ones. devtools::load_all() builds without NDEBUG, which brings assert() and upb’s unreachable-failure path back. Judge symbols and compiled-code NOTEs on an R CMD INSTALL build; test-symbols.R skips dev builds.

Continuous integration

The package calls r-actions’ r-cmd-check.yml@v1, coverage.yml and cran-release.yml (both pinned to a commit), and from native-checks.yaml the sanitizers, valgrind, LTO, gctorture, rchk, analyzers and cran-special workflows. Its own workflows:

  • conformance.yaml: protobuf’s conformance suite, built from the vendored tag, on pushes, pull requests and weekly.
  • hardening.yaml: every fuzz target’s canary must crash, then r-actions’ fuzz.yml runs each target under libFuzzer, ASan and UBSan, five minutes a target on pull requests and pushes and an hour nightly. fuzz_decode and fuzz_json reach upb through the shim alone; fuzz_build embeds R to reach the code that builds R values and the encoder that walks them.
  • vendor.yaml: r-actions’ vendor.yml, which runs tools/verify-vendor.
  • vendor-upstream.yaml: weekly, opens or updates an issue when protobuf releases a newer tag than the vendored one.

The local jobs in conformance, hardening and vendor are gated by changes.yml. Deliberate deviations from .claude/shared/ci.md:

  • coverage and pkgdown ignore CRAN-SUBMISSION by paths-ignore, because they run on documentation changes on purpose.
  • A push to main runs the full profile. The callers pass quick only for a pull request without full-ci, not profile: auto. Don’t wait on the full run a merge starts.
  • pkgdown.yaml is the scaffold’s own r-lib workflow, not an r-actions caller.

Commit CRAN-SUBMISSION on a branch and merge its pull request without [skip ci]: every other workflow skips that change, and the push to main is what runs cran-release.yaml.

Vendored native code

upb, as protobuf’s checked-in Ruby amalgamation (src/vendor/upb/ruby-upb.{c,h}), plus utf8_range (src/vendor/utf8_range/), at protobuf v36.2 (BSD-3-Clause and MIT; inst/COPYRIGHTS). src/vendor/PROVENANCE records the tag, commit, upstream hashes and patch series (tools/patches/0001 to 0008). tools/vendor-upb <tag> re-vendors, tools/verify-vendor (run by the vendor workflow) checks “upstream plus exactly these patches”, and tools/make-pedantic-patch regenerates 0003-pedantic.patch. Design §9 says why each patch exists.

  • Never hand-edit src/vendor/. Change a patch in tools/patches/ and re-run tools/vendor-upb, or tools/verify-vendor fails.
